surfaces.part: paddy ground tile (soil bank strip at top, green paddy field below)

answer.evidence: The candidate is a full 16x16 opaque terrain tile (width 16 on rows 0-15). Rows 0-2 form a brown soil bank with a dark shadow line at row 2. Rows 3-15 are a textured green paddy surface with a repeating pattern of light and dark pixels, which reads as flat ground. There is no standing volume, no ellipse, no roof and no front-edge line with eave shadow. It is a flat ground tile and not a standing object, so the kind matches terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny patch (about 16x16 px, roughly one tile) showing a paddy bank with a soil/grass strip and a darker band. Its 12 distinct colours are far below the grass reference's 80, and its 12 colours per tile is under half the grass reference's 26. The 0% flat-fill figure and 0% neutral dark edges are fine, so the outline is tinted and not near-black. The shading is shallow, at about 3 steps per material against roughly 5 on the references. The texture is limited to a few dots and stripes, with none of the clumped tufts or grain variation of the grass reference. The piece also reads as a small sticker-like block and not a 4x3 tile ground patch with the reference's variation and richness. Compared with the grass reference it is thinner and flatter, so it fails.
